text:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a GPTQ sweep across Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B this morning. focused on 4-bit GPTQ variants (per-channel, per-group tuning) and AWQ-8 baseline. seeing some consistent accuracy deltas on conversational evals for Qwen and a surprising Mistral LLM-ground truth shift. attaching top-line notes below. :eyes:

raul: awesome, thx. can you paste the top-line numbers?

maya: pasted snippet from the notebook run:```
Top-line (delta vs FP16)
Model            | GPTQ-4 (mean) | AWQ-8 (mean)
Llama-2-13B      | -1.5%         | -0.7%
Mistral-7B       | -3.8%         | -1.0%
Qwen-7B          | -6.2%         | -2.3%  <-- notable
Bench suites: conv-bench (chatbench), instruct-eval, LLM-qa (openbook style)
Notes: GPTQ-4 used group_size=128, per-channel stat smoothing=0.01
```

devin: Qwen -6.2% is big. is that across all tasks or concentrated?

maya: concentrated on multi-turn chatbench and open-ended reasoning prompts. on static QA it's -2 to -3. the chatbench failure mode looks like shorter answers or hallucinated facts.

jenny: do we have logs comparing logits between FP16 and GPTQ for failing prompts? might be kv-cache or position bias issue.

maya: i inspected token-level divergence for a few examples — divergence spikes at turn boundaries. suspect serialization of past-key-values in our conversion pipeline (we're using our internal gptq-convert v0.9).

kai: fwiw AWQ-8 behaves much closer to FP16 for Qwen in these chat cases?

maya: yes AWQ-8 is consistently ~2x better (smaller delta) for Qwen on chatbench; for Mistral GPTQ-4 still underperforms AWQ-8 but both drop more than Llama.

raul: any differences in tokenization or special-system-msg handling across families? Qwen has some special control tokens that might be affected by quantization scale mismatch.

maya: looked at tokenizer alignment — no mismatches. suspicion still around conversion of rotary embeddings handling in Qwen GPTQ kernels — might be an implementation mismatch in the quantized attention kernel (rotary scaling factor not preserved).

ci-bot: CI note — reproducer created: https://redwood-internal/pipelines/gptq/qwen-rotary-repro (run id: 2026-03-18_gptq_sweep_42) :white_check_mark:

devin: good. what's the plan for deployment profile recommendations? for Dedicated vs Hosted we need conservative defaults.

maya: proposing the following starters for rollout (subject to further tests):
- Hosted (fast path): provide AWQ-8 variant as default for Qwen-7B and Mistral-7B; expose GPTQ-4 as "experimental" with clear perf/regression warnings.
- Dedicated: allow ops teams to opt-in to GPTQ-4 if latency/cost delta is critical; require canary traffic (5%) + 48h quality gating run (chatbench + eval set).
- Private/on-prem: ship both conversion scripts but mark GPTQ-4 as "needs verification"; include conversion checksum to detect rotary mismatch.

jenny: can we add a lightweight automatic check during conversion that runs 10 seed prompts and compares token-level alignment to FP16? that would catch the big deltas quickly.

maya: yes — already added a preflight in the repro. it runs 20 short conversational traces and fails conversion if divergence > 5% on token overlap.

raul: for immediate next steps: 1) file a small PR in gptq-convert to preserve rotary scaling 2) re-run Qwen sweep with per-group_size=64 and smoothing grid {0.01,0.001} 3) add conversion preflight to pipeline. anyone object?

kai: sounds good. i'll queue the PR review and link the kernel tests.

devin: let's also log the perf / cost numbers (tokens/sec and GPU cost per 1M tokens) for AWQ/GPTQ so PM/sales can decide default pricing/commits.

maya: added perf numbers to repro:```
Perf (tokens/sec / p100 equiv)
Model      | FP16   | AWQ-8  | GPTQ-4
Llama-13B  | 1200   | 1500   | 1950
Mistral-7B | 1400   | 1700   | 2200
Qwen-7B    | 1100   | 1450   | 2100
Estimated cost reduction (GPTQ-4 vs FP16): ~45% on GPU hours
```

jenny: perfect. please tag me on the PR for the preflight addition.

maya: will do. i'll also attach a short set of failing prompts in the repro so model team can reproduce. thanks all — will update thread after kernel PR lands. :thumbsup:
